title: Context Layer
summary: Right context at the right time — from the app, not user memory

sections.heading: Orientation — Lesson Start
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? How to provide AI with the right context — at the right time — so that any feature in your product responds for «you» and not for «anyone else».
- Why now? Prompt and Style without Context = generic responses. The user feels that the assistant doesn't understand them.
- What after the lesson? You will write Context for one AI feature in a product you imagine.

sections.heading: Tension — Clear Question — Stupid Response
sections.subtitle: Clear Question — Stupid Response
sections.contentMarkdown:
- «Create a content plan» — and the response is a generic copied plan not for your project.
- The problem is not the question — the problem is that the AI doesn't know: Who are you? For whom? How much? On which platform?
- In any AI application — the context you provide (user profile, stage, last action) = the difference between a «helper» and a «wall».

sections.heading: Core Idea — The Right Context at the Right Time
sections.subtitle: The Right Context at the Right Time
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Context = all the information that the AI sees before responding: Who you are, what your project is, what happened before.
- Imagine a doctor with your file versus a doctor seeing you for the first time. Same question — different response.
- In Builder: It’s not necessary for the user to write the context every time — you pass it from the app (page, role, data).
- The rule: Background before the request. The clearer the context — the more actionable the output.

sections.heading: Comparison — General Question vs Full Context
sections.subtitle: General Question vs Full Context
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Without Context | Context Before the Request |
|-----------|----------------|
| «Create a content plan.» — the AI guesses. Generic plan — not for your project | «I am a bakery owner in Cairo, budget 2000/month, target audience women 30–45 on Instagram. 4-week plan.» — a plan you can implement |

sections.heading: Screenshot Block (Intent)
sections.contentMarkdown: Context appears before the question: Before you write — the assistant knows which path and which lesson. This context makes the response complete your journey — not generic answers. The same idea in any product: pass to the AI what the user is «in» now.

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: You want AI to help you with a marketing plan. What is the best first step?
Provide details about the project, client, and budget before the request.
Ask «Write a marketing plan» and that's it.
Ask general questions about marketing.
Explanation: Background before the request — this is what you will design in any AI feature in your product.

sections.heading: Mission — Context for One AI Feature
sections.subtitle: Context for One AI Feature
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Imagine a product with one AI feature — write the context that the app should pass. 10–15 minutes. Delivery: 1. The feature (example: «Meal Suggestions», «Support Response», «Report Summary»)
2. 4 context fields that the app passes automatically: - From the user (role/type) - From the project/product - From the session (last action) - From the stage (any screen)
3. Complete prompt example (context + short user question) Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Context from the app | 60% | 4 realistic fields — not that the user writes them every time; the feature is clear |
| Complete prompt | 40% | Context before the question; the expected response seems «personalized» |
